evidence.note: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py + tests/test_driver_packs.py landed on ddflow/DRV-packs: layered descriptor/model pack loading (packaged/user/project/local), operator-only split (headless.argv, probe refused from a cloned project), digest-pinned company packs (bare URL refused), schema version gate. tests/test_driver_packs.py passes.
D-DRV-5, D-DRV-Q5, D-config-layer-order applied; r-adapters (http via adapters.http, env via adapters.env), r-bounded-everything (MAX_PACK_BYTES).

chunk_findings.detail: `descriptor_dirs` places the “local” layer at `root/.ddflow/local/harnesses.d` — inside the cloned project tree — while `_layer_descriptors` refuses operator-only keys only when `layer == "project"`. A cloned project can therefore include `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d/evil.toml` with `schema = 2` and `[headless] argv = ["sh", "-c", "touch pwned"]` or `[probe]`; `load_descriptors(root)` parses and merges it without `PackError` because it is read as layer `"local"`, defeating the guarantee that a cloned project cannot add a key that runs a process.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:descriptor_dirs / _layer_descriptors

chunk_findings.detail: `load_pack` never calls `require_known_schema`, even though it loads a company descriptor pack and the module states each pack file carries `schema = N`. A pack containing `schema = 999\n[foo]\n` and a valid digest is returned as `{"schema": 999, ...}` instead of raising `PackError`. A newer, unreadable schema shape is handed to consumers instead of being refused as “unavailable: upgrade ddflow”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:load_pack

chunk_findings.detail: `load_pack` does not enforce that company packs are “data only”: it never calls `operator_only_violations`. A company pack with `schema = 2`, `id = "c"`, `rank = 10`, and `[headless] argv = ["sh", "-c", "malicious"]` or `[probe]` is returned as raw tables. If those raw tables are later fed into descriptor parsing, a company data pack can smuggle a process-running key that the operator-only split is supposed to forbid.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:load_pack

chunk_findings.detail: `test_shipped_descriptors_load_with_no_extra_layers` calls `DP.load_descriptors(tmp_path)` without isolating the user layer (no empty `user_home` and no `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` monkeypatch). On a machine where any file exists in the user harnesses.d directory (for example `[REDACTED:path]`), `load_descriptors` merges that user descriptor into the result, so the returned list is not equal to `harnessreg.load()` and the test fails even though the code is correct. The same un-isolated call pattern also affects the project-layer tests around lines 81, 88, and 95.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_packs.py:113

chunk_findings.detail: Only `layer == "project"` is refused for operator-only keys, but `load_descriptors` still treats `{root}/.ddflow/local/harnesses.d` as the operator “local” layer. A clone that contains `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d/evil.toml` with `[headless]\nargv = ["malware"]` (or a top-level `[probe]` argv) is parsed by `harnessreg.parse` and returned from `load_descriptors` with a process-launch key, which breaks the “cloned project cannot add launch argv” rule. The same file under `.ddflow/harnesses.d` is correctly rejected.

chunk_findings.detail: Company packs are specified as data-only (`OPERATOR_ONLY` even names a company data pack as a layer that must not set a process key) and every file must refuse a schema newer than `CURRENT_SCHEMA`. `load_pack` never calls `operator_only_violations` or `require_known_schema`. A digest-matching URL or local TOML with `schema = 99` and `[headless] argv = ["curl", "evil"]` is returned as a dict instead of `PackError`, so the content is not kept out.

chunk_findings.detail: A cloned repository can bypass the project-layer operator-only check by placing the malicious descriptor in `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d`. `load_descriptors` reads that directory as layer `"local"`, and `_layer_descriptors` only calls `operator_only_violations` when `layer == "project"`. So a clone containing `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d/pwn.toml` with `[headless] argv = ["sh","-c","id"]` is parsed and returned as a launch descriptor, directly breaking the promise/test that a cloned project cannot add launch argv.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:load_descriptors

chunk_findings.detail: `load_pack` documents a company pack as “data only” but does not refuse `[headless] argv` or `[probe]`. Given a pinned remote pack whose TOML contains `[headless] argv = ["sh","-c","id"]`, the function fetches it, accepts the matching digest, and returns that process-running table without ever calling `operator_only_violations`. A company data pack can therefore carry a launch command, violating the operator-only split.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:load_pack

chunk_findings.detail: The test is not isolated from the user layer. It only passes an empty `tmp_path`, but `DP.load_descriptors(tmp_path)` defaults the user layer from the real user environment (the same default the suite takes care to monkeypatch in `test_descriptor_dirs_names_all_four_layers`). On any developer or CI runner that already has a descriptor in the user `harnesses.d`, `DP.load_descriptors(tmp_path)` will include that extra descriptor and therefore will not equal `harnessreg.load()`, making the test fail even when the implementation is correct.

chunk_findings.detail: The operator-only argv/probe refusal runs only when the layer name is `"project"`. chunk_findings.detail: `Path.read_text()` returns a `str`, but `DP.content_digest` is written for the bytes content `load_pack` reads and hashes; the existing `test_content_digest_is_sha256_hex` exercises it only with `b"x"`, and `hashlib.sha256` does not accept `str`. As a result each new test passes a `str` to `DP.content_digest`, producing `TypeError: Unicode-objects must be encoded before hashing` before `DP.load_pack` is reached, so these tests error rather than exercising the digest-pinned data-only/schema refusal behavior.

A broken implementation that drops the project layer is therefore not caught in that environment; the test should isolate the user layer with `user_home=tmp_path / "user"` so only the project descriptor can satisfy it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_layer_descriptors` reads every `.toml` in a layer with `p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` and never enforces `MAX_PACK_BYTES`. The project layer `.ddflow/harnesses.d` is controlled by a cloned repository, and Git can commit a symlink such as `.ddflow/harnesses.d/huge.toml -> /dev/zero`; `load_descriptors(root)` then blocks/OOMs reading it instead of refusing it as larger than `MAX_PACK_BYTES` (whose comment says a larger body than this is not a descriptor pack). This violates the bounded-pack property and allows a malicious clone to DoS `load_descriptors`.

chunk_findings.detail: The test expects `PackError` for `[headless] argv` in `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d`. That directory is the gitignored machine-local operator layer, and D-DRV-Q5 restricts only the project layer `.ddflow/harnesses.d`; a legitimate operator-local descriptor should be allowed to set a launch key. Given `tmp_path/.ddflow/local/harnesses.d/demo.toml` with `headless.argv`, rejecting it either makes the implementation refuse valid operator configuration or makes this test fail against a correct implementation. This contradicts the operator-only split and the cloned-project threat model.

chunk_findings.detail: A per-repo file that never writes an operator-only key still comes back with a process launch. The comment on `_layer_descriptors` says `harnessreg.parse` substitutes a default argv unless an explicit empty `argv` is refused first, but the refusal only runs when the key is present (`operator_only_violations`) and the parsed object is returned unchanged. Given `.ddflow/harnesses.d/custom.toml` with `schema = 2`, a new `id`/`rank`, and no `[headless]`/`[probe]`, `operator_only_violations` is empty, `parse` fills the default argv, and `load_descriptors` returns that `Harness`. The same file with an existing shipped id replaces the operator descriptor entirely, so the clone’s default argv is what would run. That is a launch command that did not come from the shipped set or the user layer.

The test constructs `probing` as `_GOOD + '
[probe]
argv = [["demo", "--version"]]
'`, which TOML-parses into `{"probe": {"argv": [["demo", "--version"]]}}`—a `probe` table—not the root-level `probe` array that the file's own `test_probe_is_operator_only` establishes as the violation shape (`{"probe": [["claude", "--version"]]}`). chunk_findings.detail: `load_pack` applies `operator_only_violations` to the entire raw TOML document, but that function only inspects the root table for `headless` and `probe`. A company descriptor pack is the raw top-level tables (the function returns them, and a pack can name multiple descriptors), so a file such as `schema = 2`, `[evil]`, `[evil.headless]`, `argv = ["sh", "-c", "evil"]` parses to `{"schema": 2, "evil": {"headless": {"argv": ...}}}`; `operator_only_violations` sees no top-level `headless`/`probe` and returns `[]`, so `load_pack` returns the pack. The process-running key is not refused despite the data-only split, and downstream merging of those raw tables could execute it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:load_pack

chunk_findings.detail: `_layer_descriptors` iterates `sorted(directory.glob("*.toml"))` but does not filter to files. A cloned project can make `.ddflow/harnesses.d/boom.toml/` an actual directory by tracking a file inside it; `Path.glob` yields that directory, `_read_bounded` then calls `Path.open("rb")` on it and raises an uncaught `IsADirectoryError`, aborting `load_descriptors` instead of skipping or raising a `PackError`.

chunk_findings.detail: On Windows, `Path.write_text(_GOOD)` writes in text mode with `newline=None`, translating `\n` to `\r\n`; the bytes on disk are not the bytes of `_GOOD`. Since pack digest verification hashes the file’s bytes (as `test_content_digest_is_sha256_hex` hashes bytes), `DP.content_digest(_GOOD)` is the wrong digest and `DP.load_pack(str(p), digest=DP.content_digest(_GOOD))` raises `PackError("digest mismatch")` even though the pack content is correct. The same text-write/digest-mismatch pattern also affects `test_a_company_pack_is_data_only` and `test_a_pack_with_a_newer_schema_is_refused`, making the digest-pinned pack tests non-portable.

chunk_findings.detail:
The operator-only split is keyed to the layer name: `_layer_descriptors` only calls `operator_only_violations` when `layer == "project"`. But `descriptor_dirs` puts the local layer at `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "harnesses.d"`, which is also inside the cloned project directory. A malicious clone can therefore ship the very same executable descriptor under `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d/evil.toml`:
```toml
schema = 2
[headless]
argv = ["sh", "-c", "echo pwned"]
```
`load_descriptors(root)` loads it as `"local"`, skips the project-layer operator-only check, calls `harnessreg.parse`, and returns that `Harness`. The documented test goal was that a cloned project cannot add launch argv; placing the file in `.ddflow/local/harnesses.d` defeats this because only the `"project"` directory is treated as untrusted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:_layer_descriptors

chunk_findings.detail: `operator_only_violations` only treats `headless` as operator-only when it is a dict. A company pack or project descriptor whose TOML is `schema = 2` plus `[[headless]]` / `argv = ["sh", "-c", "evil"]` (or `[[evil.headless]]` under an array-of-tables descriptor) parses to `headless` as a list of tables, the `"argv" in headless` check is skipped, and the nested dicts only have `argv`, so the walk returns `[]`. `load_pack` then returns that raw document, and `_layer_descriptors` does not raise, so the launch argv the check claims to refuse is admitted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverpacks.py:operator_only_violations

chunk_findings.detail: `_read_bounded` decodes with bare `.decode("utf-8")` and `require_known_schema` / the project-layer check call `tomllib.loads` with no handler. A cloned `.ddflow/harnesses.d/boom.toml` of bytes `b"\xff"` (or invalid TOML such as `b"["`) makes `load_descriptors` raise `UnicodeDecodeError` or `TOMLDecodeError` instead of `PackError` or skipping the entry, so one non-descriptor file aborts the whole load.
